response: Routine intraoperative frozen-section examination of sentinel lymph nodes in breast cancer may be worthwhile, but its benefit depends on the size of the tumor. For patients with smaller invasive cancers, routine intraoperative frozen-section examination may not be necessary. However, as the tumor size increases, the benefit of routine intraoperative frozen-section examination also increases, particularly in detecting micrometastatic disease. Therefore, it is essential to consider the individual patient's circumstances and tumor characteristics when deciding whether to perform routine intraoperative frozen-section examination of sentinel lymph nodes in breast cancer.
